page: Vultr vx1-m-8c-64g-480s is a memory-optimized instance in the VX1 Cloud Compute line. Powered by dedicated AMD EPYC processors running at a base clock of 2.0 GHz, the instance delivers 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system features 64 GB of system RAM, providing an 8 GB per vCPU allocation ratio, and is paired with a bundled 480 GB NVMe solid-state drive for high-speed local data persistence. It operates on the x86_64 architecture with hardware instruction support for AVX-512, SHA-NI, and AES cryptography, while omitting discrete graphics hardware.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded and integer-focused execution. The instance scores in the top tier for single-core stress-ng tests, single-threaded gzip compression at 39.69 GB/sec, single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 17.7 GB/sec, and Geekbench text processing. Multi-core performance metrics, such as PassMark CPU (18,514.04), Geekbench multi-core (7,489.0), and multi-threaded decompression, sit within average tiers. Memory subsystem benchmarks show uncached read speeds of 71.86 GB/sec and write speeds of 41.17 GB/sec, supporting Redis workloads at 15.3 million SET operations per second and static web throughput of 26.44 GB/sec.

The 1:8 vCPU-to-memory configuration delivers balanced cost efficiency for tasks requiring substantial in-memory capacity without necessitating high core density. However, compute scaling shows limits on heavy multi-core throughput and larger machine learning workloads, as reflected in weaker prompt-processing benchmarks for 7B parameter models. The bundled local NVMe storage and high memory headroom position the vx1-m-8c-64g-480s effectively for in-memory databases, Redis caches, batch data transformation, and moderate application hosting.
description: Vultr vx1-m-8c-64g-480s is a memory-optimized cloud server within the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 AMD EPYC physical cores clocked at 2.0 GHz, alongside 64 GB of RAM and 480 GB of local NVMe storage on an x86_64 architecture. The server provides an 8 GB per vCPU memory footprint without hardware GPU acceleration. Benchmark profiles indicate top-tier single-core compute and data compression throughput, while overall multi-threaded throughput and memory bandwidth fall into mid-range tiers. The server handles key-value caching efficiently, sustaining 15.3 million Redis operations per second. While larger AI inference tasks show performance trade-offs due to modest core counts, the generous memory capacity and local NVMe storage make the vx1-m-8c-64g-480s well suited for in-memory caching systems, transactional databases, and memory-intensive backend services.
